preamble: Replacement of glottalization by pharyngealization: the alveolar ejective [tʼ] becomes the pharyngealized stop [tˤ]. Proto-Semitic emphatic *ṭ, reconstructed as *tʼ, stays ejective in Geʽez (ጠ) and modern Ethiopian Semitic but is pharyngealized in Arabic ṭāʾ and in traditional pronunciations of Hebrew and Aramaic ṭēt. Blau (2010) argues that pre-exilic Hebrew ṭēt was still ejective, placing the change within recorded Hebrew history. The ejective starting point is a reconstruction: Watson (2002: 2) notes that eighth-century descriptions suggest velarized emphatics in Classical Arabic, while 'a glottalized articulation of the emphatics is generally reconstructed for Proto-Semitic'.

examples.note: Geʽez ጠሐነ ṭäḥänä, Tigrinya ṭäḥanä and Harari ṭäḥana keep ejective [tʼ].
Ejective value per Blau (2010); Ashkenazi, Sephardi and Israeli Hebrew later merged ṭ with plain t.
